chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Do not strike your faces with water when you perform wudu (ablution), but rather pour the water gently.”

Because the way to reconcile the two is that the first report is understood as indicating the permissibility of that, and that its opposite is not obligatory; while the second is understood to mean that something else is preferable. Thus, there is no contradiction between them on this basis.

key_terms.الْأَوْلَى: that which is more preferable or better
key_terms.وُجُوهَكُمْ: your faces, meaning the part washed in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How should water be applied to the face during wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns the proper manner of washing the face in wudu (ablution), teaching that one should not splash or strike the face with water harshly but rather apply it gently. The accompanying note explains that reports on this issue are reconciled by understanding one as indicating permissibility and the other as indicating what is more preferable in practice.
